source.title: On Cohen–Macaulay modules over non-commutative surface singularities

actual_fresh_read: Definitions and noncommutative normal/terminal/regular setup, printed2–5. Referenced Chan–Ingalls resolution and order-theoretic normality facts remain Known.
Theorem2.1, Lemma2.5, Proposition2.7, Proposition2.8, Corollary2.9 and Proposition2.10: entire displayed statements and complete written proofs, printed5–9.

Lemma2.11, Proposition2.12 and Theorem2.13: entire displayed statements and complete written proofs, printed9–12, including all local-cohomology embeddings, the injective boundary criterion, projective nilpotent lifting, reduction-cycle orbit argument and uniqueness.
Corollary2.14 and Theorem3.3 statements/explicit proof-omission notices: no fresh proof audit is claimed for these omitted arguments.
checked_scope: Global generation in the paper is generation as an order-module; Remark2.2 explicitly distinguishes ordinary O-module generation.
The weak reduction cycle requires a locally bi-principal ideal, generic module generation of I/I² and H1(I/I²)=0; the stronger cycle also requires generic generation of the dual canonical module.
Proposition2.10 chooses I=B(-nD) by an unspecified sufficiently large Serre twist depending on the chosen order. It supplies no uniform-in-period/rank or cover-degree value of n.

Theorem2.13 gives ground-field formal effectivity and, under the stronger cycle condition, uniqueness for full order-modules. It supplies neither an all-coefficient polynomial atlas nor the needed coordinate/equation budget.
current_unproved_inputs: Uniform reduction depth and ordinary/coherent cohomology for the selected canonical-stable order
Uniform small order-module generators and short syzygies for every counted object
Compatibility of these choices with fixed Frobenius pole losses and exact finite-family effectivity
